description: B2 ROOF at 8/12 from ONE loft.roof 1.0.0 custom feature (ROOF; docs/reference-parts/buildings.md B2 roof, its pitch edit): a gable on walls whose outer faces are Y 0 and Y 120 with top plates at Z 97.125 and 3.5 deep, 144 along the ridge, pitch 8/12, 2x6 rafters at 24 in o.c. with a 12 in level overhang, a 2x8 ridge board, all spf_lumber. model.json is EXACTLY the plugin's expansion with the member materials documents applies; members.json is each body's member metadata. packages/loft-plugins/tests/test_roof.py asserts both files are the plugin's output; services/geometry/tests/test_roof_b2.py checks the cut list, the exported STEP against an independent build123d script, and interference with the walls. Each rafter is one side profile on a YZ plane at its X, extruded 1.5 along +X; the ridge is its section on YZ extruded 144.
derivation: Every expectation except the mesh counts is ANALYTIC, from buildings.md's numbers, never from the plugin. In the front rafter's (Y, Z) frame: slope = 8/12; a full seat would make a 3.5 x 8/12 = 2.333 heel, over the 1/3-depth limit, so the heel is 5.5/3 = 1.8333 and the seat 1.8333 / (8/12) = 2.75; the bottom edge is Z = 97.125 + (Y - seat) x slope; the plumb depth is 5.5 x sqrt(1 + slope^2) = 6.61017733835; the ridge face is Y 60 - 0.75 = 59.25. Profile (tail bottom, heel bottom, heel top, seat inner, ridge bottom, ridge top, tail top): (-12, 87.2916666667), (0, 95.2916666667), (0, 97.125), (2.75, 97.125), (59.25, 134.791666667), (59.25, 141.401844005), (-12, 93.901844005). The back rafter is its mirror about Y 60. Rafter centres X 0.75, 24, 48, 72, 96, 120, 143.25 (7 pairs, 14 rafters, 1.5 thick).
line length = (12 + 59.25) x sqrt(1 + slope^2) = 85.631843 in (buildings.md: 85.632); overall length (long point to long point, the cut list's) = line + 5.5 x slope = 89.298509 in.

profile area (shoelace) = 468.454302024 in^2; rafter volume = 1.5 x area = 702.681453036 in^3; ridge = 144 x 1.5 x 7.25 = 1566 in^3, Z 134.151844005..141.401844005 (top flush with the rafters' top at its face). volume = 14 x rafter + ridge = 11403.5403425 in^3; x 25.4^3 = 186870545.419247 mm^3.
centroid = volume-weighted mean: x = 72 in = 1828.8 mm and y = 60 in = 1524 mm (symmetric); z from the profile's centroid (shoelace) and the ridge's centre.
mass_g = volume x 450 kg/m^3 (spf_lumber, every body by its member material); center_of_mass = centroid (one density).
bounding_box: X 0..144, Y -12..132 (the tails), Z 87.2916666667 (tail bottom) .. 141.401844005 (ridge top) in.
topology: 14 heptagonal prisms x (9 faces, 21 edges) + 1 box (6, 12) = 132 faces, 306 edges, 15 shells.
MESH counts are recorded, and exact for planar prisms: a rafter is 2 heptagons x 5 triangles + 7 quads x 2 = 24 triangles on 2 x 7 + 7 x 4 = 42 vertices, a box 12 on 24: 348 triangles, 612 vertices.
tolerance_rationale: Measured first, then set (geometry-gates skill): the bounds are ABSOLUTE and the part is ~1.8e8 mm^3 summed over 15 separate bodies; the kernel differs from the analytic sums by 3.6e-7 mm^3 on the volume, 2e-8 mm^2 on the area and <= 1e-12 mm on the centroid. 1e-6 is ~5e-15 relative; a rafter 0.001 in out of place along its slope moves the volume by > 10 mm^3.
roundtrip_tolerance_rationale: KERNEL-LEVEL, measured 2026-10-17: OCCT's STEP writer rounds the sloped rafters' irrational coordinates, so each re-imported rafter moves by ~2.5e-5 mm^3 (~2e-12 relative). Round-trip drift: volume -2.33e-4 mm^3 and area -8.0e-6 mm^2 (plugin), -1.9e-5 / +1.8e-6 (twin); centroid <= 1.4e-9 mm. The independent PURE build123d twin (test_roof_b2.script_roof, exported with build123d's own export_step) drifts the same way (the 6/12 twin by the identical -3.47e-4), so it is OCCT's STEP, not Loft's export. 1e-3 is 2.9x the worst and applies to volume and area only; the centroid and bounds keep ROUNDTRIP_TOL. The B1 deck's boxes have exact decimal coordinates, hence its smaller bound.
